All arithmetic is modulo 19.

1) One-to-one: f is not one-to-one. Counterexample: f(3)=3^3+8*3=27+24=51≡13 (mod 19), while f(5)=5^3+8*5=125+40=165≡13 (mod 19). Since 3≠5, distinct inputs give the same encoded residue.

2) Original inputs that give recorded residue 13: f(3)=13, f(5)=13, and f(11)=11^3+8*11=1331+88=1419≡13 (mod 19), since 19*74=1406. The polynomial x^3+8x-13 has degree 3 over the field Z/19Z, so it has at most three roots. The three distinct roots already found are therefore all roots. Thus the possible original inputs for output 13 are {3,5,11}.

3) Value table x -> f(x) for x=0,...,18:
0->0, 1->9, 2->5, 3->13, 4->1, 5->13, 6->17, 7->0, 8->6, 9->3, 10->16, 11->13, 12->0, 13->2, 14->6, 15->18, 16->6, 17->14, 18->10.
The output set is {0,1,2,3,5,6,9,10,13,14,16,17,18}. Hence the residues this device can never output are {4,7,8,11,12,15}.

4) For d(x)=3x^2+8, if d(x)=0 then 3x^2+8≡0, so 3x^2≡11. Since 3^{-1}≡13 because 3*13=39≡1 (mod 19), this gives x^2≡11*13=143≡10 (mod 19). The quadratic residues modulo 19 are {0,1,4,5,6,7,9,11,16,17}; 10 is not among them. Therefore x^2≡10 has no solution, and d(x) is nonzero for every allowed x in {0,1,...,18}. In particular, the objections' check at x=7 is incorrect: 7^2=49≡11, not 10, so d(7)=3*49+8=155≡3 (mod 19), not 0; similarly d(12)=3*144+8=440≡3 (mod 19).

dispositions.reason: The objection's arithmetic is wrong: 7^2=49 and 19*2=38, so 49≡11 (mod 19), not 10. The listed quadratic residues {0,1,4,5,6,7,9,11,16,17} are correct and omit 10. Thus x^2≡10 has no solution, and the working answer's derivative conclusion is not invalidated.

This objection depends on the false congruence 7^2≡10. Actually 7^2≡11. Hence d(7)=3*49+8=155≡3 (mod 19), not 0, and d(12)=3*144+8=440≡3 (mod 19), not 0. The derivative condition is x^2≡10, which has no solution modulo 19, so d(x) is nonzero at every allowed x.

BEGIN PROBLEM (870 characters)
A device encodes one residue x from the set {0,1,...,18} as f(x) = x^3 + 8x modulo 19. Remainders are always chosen in {0,1,...,18}. All additions, products, and equalities in the encoding are modulo 19.

Determine whether f is one-to-one on the stated residue set. Separately, determine whether the polynomial d(x) = 3x^2 + 8 is nonzero at every allowed x. Give proofs or explicit counterexamples with the arithmetic that establishes each finding. Also list every possible original input when the recorded encoded residue is 13, and list all residues that this device can never output. These lists are part of the requested answer. A formal derivative here means the displayed polynomial d(x).

Reason in prose from this problem. No code execution, calculators, external tools, or retrieval are available. Give the exact final facts and a checkable public explanation.

END PROBLEM

BEGIN WORKING ANSWER (1336 characters)
All arithmetic is modulo 19.

One-to-one: No. Counterexample: f(3)=3^3+8*3=27+24=51≡13 (mod 19), and f(5)=5^3+8*5=125+40=165≡13 (mod 19). Since 3≠5, f is not one-to-one.

Preimages of 13: f(3)=13, f(5)=13, and f(11)=11^3+8*11=1331+88=1419≡13 (mod 19). The polynomial x^3+8x-13 is a nonzero cubic over the field Z/19Z, so it has at most three roots; the three distinct roots already found are therefore all roots. Thus original inputs giving recorded residue 13 are {3,5,11}.

Full value table x -> f(x) for x=0..18:
0->0, 1->9, 2->5, 3->13, 4->1, 5->13, 6->17, 7->0, 8->6, 9->3, 10->16, 11->13, 12->0, 13->2, 14->6, 15->18, 16->6, 17->14, 18->10.
The set of outputs is {0,1,2,3,5,6,9,10,13,14,16,17,18}. Hence the residues never output are {4,7,8,11,12,15}.

Derivative check: d(x)=3x^2+8. If d(x)=0 then 3x^2+8≡0, so 3x^2≡11. Since 3^{-1}≡13 because 3*13=39≡1, we get x^2≡11*13=143≡10 (mod 19). The quadratic residues mod 19 are {0,1,4,5,6,7,9,11,16,17}; 10 is not in that set. Therefore x^2≡10 has no solution, and d(x) is nonzero for every x in {0,...,18}.

Assumption/uncertainty: I assume the allowed inputs are exactly the residues 0 through 18 and that all computations are mod 19. No arithmetic uncertainty remains; note that d(x) being nonzero everywhere does not make f injective, as the explicit collision f(3)=f(5)=13 shows.
END WORKING ANSWER

BEGIN OBJECTION c0001-k01-o001 (344 characters)
The claim that '10 is not in that set' of quadratic residues modulo 19 is incorrect. The working answer lists the quadratic residues as {0,1,4,5,6,7,9,11,16,17} but omits 10. Direct calculation shows 7^2 = 49 = 2*19 + 10, so 7^2 ≡ 10 (mod 19). Thus 10 is a quadratic residue. This error invalidates the derivation that x^2 ≡ 10 has no solution.
END OBJECTION c0001-k01-o001

BEGIN DEFEATS c0001-k01-o001 (66 characters)
The conclusion that d(x) = 3x^2 + 8 is nonzero at every allowed x.
END DEFEATS c0001-k01-o001

Awaiting operative return.
END DISPOSITION REASON c0001-k01-o001

BEGIN OBJECTION c0001-k01-o002 (466 characters)
Because 10 is a quadratic residue (specifically 7^2 ≡ 10 and (-7)^2 ≡ 12^2 ≡ 10), the equation x^2 ≡ 10 has solutions x ≡ 7 and x ≡ 12. Substituting these into d(x): d(7) = 3(49) + 8 ≡ 3(10) + 8 = 38 ≡ 0 (mod 19). Similarly d(12) ≡ 0. The working answer's table correctly lists f(7)=0 and f(12)=0, which is consistent with a zero derivative indicating a critical point (and potential multiple root), but the explicit claim that d(x) is never zero is factually wrong.
END OBJECTION c0001-k01-o002

END DEFEATS c0001-k01-o002

unresolved
END RECORDED DISPOSITION c0001-k01-o002

END DISPOSITION REASON c0001-k01-o002
